questions.topic: Single-Shot Query Rewriting, Expansion, and HyDE
questions.question: What does a query rewriter do?
options: Transforms the raw user query into a better search query before retrieval
Rewrites each indexed document into question form during the ingest pass
Condenses the retrieved chunks into a shorter prompt before generation
Reorders the retriever's candidate list with a cross-encoder before fusion

questions.topic: Single-Shot Query Rewriting, Expansion, and HyDE
questions.question: What does HyDE embed instead of the question?
options: The previous assistant turn, treated as a standalone search query
A centroid vector built from the corpus's most frequent past queries
A short hypothetical answer that the model writes for the question
The question with corpus synonyms appended to each of its rare terms

questions.topic: Single-Shot Query Rewriting, Expansion, and HyDE
questions.question: A pipeline retrieves with four query paraphrases instead of one. What is the direct cost?
options: The index stores one extra copy of every document for each variant
Retrieval work multiplies by the number of variants that are issued
The reranker must be retrained whenever a new paraphrase is added
The embedding dimension is split across variants, coarsening each one

questions.topic: Single-Shot Query Rewriting, Expansion, and HyDE
questions.question: For which query is HyDE most likely to mislead retrieval?
options: How can I reduce latency in a hybrid search pipeline
Why does my back ache after very long haul flights
What are best practices for sharding a large index
What is the exact serial format for part ZX-4817-Q

questions.topic: Single-Shot Query Rewriting, Expansion, and HyDE
questions.question: A support product can add only one query-side transform this quarter. Which usually pays back fastest?
options: HyDE on all traffic, so every search starts from an answer-shaped passage
Single-shot rewriting that steers the query toward corpus vocabulary
Eight-variant expansion, fused with reciprocal rank fusion across the legs
A second embedding model, fused with the first over the same candidates

questions.topic: Single-Shot Query Rewriting, Expansion, and HyDE
questions.question: Why keep the raw user query after adding a rewriter?
options: It is the string the billing pipeline meters each request against
It doubles as the hypothetical document that HyDE has to embed
It supplies the online signal that keeps the rewriter itself tuned
It is the fallback to search with when a rewrite degrades results

questions.topic: Retrieval as a Tool: Search, Read, Decide-to-Stop
questions.question: What distinguishes agentic retrieval from single-shot RAG?
options: The model decides in a loop whether to search, read, or answer
An agent re-indexes the corpus between queries to sharpen recall
The retriever calls the generator once for each candidate document
Every query is expanded into paraphrases before one fused retrieval

questions.topic: Retrieval as a Tool: Search, Read, Decide-to-Stop
questions.question: What is a decide-to-stop policy?
options: The rule that truncates a retrieved document so it fits the context
The cap on how far the index may grow between two re-index runs
The criterion that ends the search loop and commits to an answer
The threshold that blocks low-quality documents at ingest time

questions.topic: Retrieval as a Tool: Search, Read, Decide-to-Stop
questions.question: An agent averages three search iterations before answering. Roughly what latency does the deliberation add?
options: Well under one second in total
Roughly three hundred milliseconds
Several seconds before generation
Essentially nothing, given caching

questions.topic: Retrieval as a Tool: Search, Read, Decide-to-Stop
questions.question: Which question should be routed to the agentic path?
options: Compare SLA terms across our three enterprise contracts
Give me the URL of our public API status page please
Reset the password on my administrator account today
Tell me which year this company was originally founded

questions.topic: Retrieval as a Tool: Search, Read, Decide-to-Stop
questions.question: An agent rephrases the same failing query nine times before timing out. What design element was missing?
options: A larger embedding model behind the semantic retrieval leg
A second search tool scoped to a different document set
A longer system prompt describing the corpus in more detail
An explicit budget cap inside the decide-to-stop policy

questions.topic: Retrieval as a Tool: Search, Read, Decide-to-Stop
questions.question: Why should search results carry stable document IDs back to the model?
options: IDs compress far better than the snippet text that they stand for
Follow-up read calls can then fetch a full document cheaply
IDs give the embedding model a stable key to cache its vectors on
They let the index skip its access-control check on repeat reads

questions.topic: Query Decomposition and Multi-hop Retrieval
questions.question: When does a question need decomposition into sub-queries?
options: When the query contains spelling errors the analyzer cannot repair
When the corpus has grown past roughly one million indexed documents
When the user writes in a language the embedding model handles poorly
When answering requires chaining facts that no single document holds

questions.topic: Query Decomposition and Multi-hop Retrieval
questions.question: In recursive multi-hop retrieval, what feeds the next sub-query?
options: A random sample of documents drawn from the first hop's results
The answer entity that the previous hop resolved from the corpus
The user's full session history, appended to the original question
The most frequent terms across the whole corpus, added as context

questions.topic: Query Decomposition and Multi-hop Retrieval
questions.question: Each hop retrieves the needed fact with probability 0.9. What is a three-hop chain's retrieval success rate?

questions.topic: Query Decomposition and Multi-hop Retrieval
questions.question: Hop one returns the wrong company. What happens in hop two?
options: Its sub-query is built on the wrong entity and drifts further away
The retriever detects the mismatch and backtracks to redo hop one
Later hops are unaffected, since each hop retrieves independently
The synthesis pass discards the chain before hop two is executed

questions.topic: Query Decomposition and Multi-hop Retrieval
questions.question: What does the least-decomposition principle advise?
options: Try one retrieval first and decompose only compositional questions
Split every question into at least three sub-queries before searching
Retrieve no more than once per session, whatever the question asks
Decompose the documents at ingest rather than the queries at runtime

questions.topic: Query Decomposition and Multi-hop Retrieval
questions.question: Why measure per-hop retrieval success separately from final answer accuracy?
options: Per-hop scores are far cheaper to compute than end-to-end accuracy
Final accuracy double-counts any hop that returned the same document
Human judges agree with one another more readily on per-hop scores
Retrieval failures and reasoning failures need entirely different fixes

questions.topic: Conversational Query Rewriting Across Turns
questions.question: What problem does conversational query rewriting solve?
options: Users who type their questions in an unsupported second language
Follow-up turns that omit the entities they are actually asking about
Documents that arrive out of chronological order during ingestion
Indexes that store single-turn text and no conversation history at all

questions.topic: Conversational Query Rewriting Across Turns
questions.question: What does the rewriter use as context?
options: Only the current user turn, held deliberately free of prior state
The corpus term dictionary, so rewrites stay inside its vocabulary
Recent history, including the assistant's own previous answer text
The user's account metadata, which names the plan being discussed

questions.topic: Conversational Query Rewriting Across Turns
questions.question: A user switches topics but retrieval keeps returning documents about the old topic. What failed?
options: The vector index kept serving stale vectors from before the switch
The rewrite over-anchored and dragged stale entities into the query
The reranker depth was set too shallow to surface the new subject
The corpus was never re-chunked after the newer documents landed

questions.topic: Conversational Query Rewriting Across Turns
questions.question: Why should low-confidence previous answers be excluded from rewrite context?
options: Their wrong entities would be injected into every rewrite that follows
Their extra length pushes the rewrite prompt past its own token budget
They rarely name any entity at all, so they add nothing to the rewrite
They decode more slowly, which delays the rewrite call on every turn

questions.topic: Conversational Query Rewriting Across Turns
questions.question: Which rewriter instruction prevents over-anchoring?
options: Always append the previous assistant answer verbatim to the turn
Rewrite every turn aggressively, even one already standalone
Return the turn unchanged whenever it is already standalone
Drop the user's turn and search over the conversation history

questions.topic: Conversational Query Rewriting Across Turns
questions.question: How should a conversational rewriter be evaluated?
options: By the average length of the final answers it leads the system to
By the index size measured before and after the rewriter shipped
By the number of prompt tokens the rewrite call consumes per turn
Against history-plus-turn pairs with a gold standalone rewrite each

questions.topic: Self-Correcting RAG: Reflect, Re-Retrieve, Refine
questions.question: What does retrieval grading check?
options: Whether the index generation is current for the corpus being served
Whether the caller is authorized to read every retrieved document
Whether the retrieved documents are relevant and sufficient to answer
Whether the drafted answer matches the product's required brand tone

questions.topic: Self-Correcting RAG: Reflect, Re-Retrieve, Refine
questions.question: What does generation reflection check?
options: That the draft cites at least one span from every retrieved document
That every claim in the draft is supported by the retrieved context
That the draft stays under the word limit the product's UI allows
That the query rewrite preserved the user's original intent exactly

questions.topic: Self-Correcting RAG: Reflect, Re-Retrieve, Refine
questions.question: What is the typical latency and token cost of a fully self-correcting pipeline versus single-pass RAG?
options: About half the cost of the single-pass baseline
About the same cost as the single-pass baseline
About ten times the cost of the single-pass baseline
About two to four times the single-pass baseline

questions.topic: Self-Correcting RAG: Reflect, Re-Retrieve, Refine
questions.question: When is it reasonable to skip the reflection gate?
options: When retrieval scores are strong and the question is a simple one
When the user is on a premium plan and expects a fast response
When the answer contains numeric values a judge cannot verify
When the corpus fits inside the judge model's own context window

questions.topic: Self-Correcting RAG: Reflect, Re-Retrieve, Refine
questions.question: After two failed re-retrieval attempts on a high-stakes support question, what should the system do?
options: Answer from the model's own memory and mark the reply unverified
Keep re-retrieving until the grader finally passes the documents
Lower the faithfulness threshold until the current draft passes it
Answer with an explicit caveat about the gap, or else abstain

questions.topic: Self-Correcting RAG: Reflect, Re-Retrieve, Refine
questions.question: Why are self-correction gates given attempt budgets rather than open loops?
options: Budgets keep the vector index from being read more than once
Bounded loops produce request traces that are far easier to parse
The checking judgments can themselves be wrong in both directions
Users have been shown to prefer shorter answers to longer ones

questions.topic: Text-to-SQL as a Retrieval Tool for Structured Data
questions.question: What does text-to-SQL add to a RAG system?
options: A path that answers structured questions by querying the warehouse
A way to store document chunks as relational rows inside a database
A replacement for the embedding model on numeric-heavy documents
An interface that lets end users type raw SQL against the corpus

questions.topic: Text-to-SQL as a Retrieval Tool for Structured Data
questions.question: What is schema linking?
options: Joining two separate databases together at query execution time
Selecting the tables and columns that belong in the generation prompt
Encrypting the schema metadata at rest so the model cannot read it
Linking each returned row back to the source document it came from

questions.topic: Text-to-SQL as a Retrieval Tool for Structured Data
questions.question: The user asks about the `Team plan`. What does value grounding provide?
options: A checksum over the generated SQL string before it is executed
The mapping from that phrase to the real plan_id values in the table
A per-tenant rate limit capping how often the warehouse is queried
An estimate of the bytes the query will scan before it is executed

questions.topic: Text-to-SQL as a Retrieval Tool for Structured Data
questions.question: Which execution guardrail is non-negotiable?
options: Letting the model create temporary tables to stage its intermediates
Running generated SQL under an admin role so that no query is ever blocked
Allowing multi-statement scripts so complex answers can be assembled
Parsing the SQL and executing only a validated single SELECT read-only

questions.topic: Text-to-SQL as a Retrieval Tool for Structured Data
questions.question: Generated SQL returns zero rows. What is the dangerous misreading?
options: Concluding the warehouse is down and failing the request outright
Concluding a table was renamed and retrying against an older schema
Reporting zero churn when the query itself asked the wrong question
Concluding the caller lacks permission on one of the joined tables

questions.topic: Text-to-SQL as a Retrieval Tool for Structured Data
questions.question: For governed business metrics, what should be preferred over free-form SQL generation?
options: Curated semantic-layer queries with documented metric definitions
A larger few-shot budget carrying more question-to-SQL exemplars
Nightly fine-tuning of the SQL model on the warehouse query logs
Direct analyst access to the raw tables behind each governed metric
